newsitem.title: MONTSERRAT: Dutch navy searches for Montserrat volcano victims.
newsitem.headline: Dutch navy searches for Montserrat volcano victims.

text.p: Dutch sailors helped in house-to-house searches on Thursday for 18 people reported missing in Montserrat, one day after an active volcano spewed hot gases and rocks over much of the Caribbean island, burning villages.
"We have airlifted to safety some 12 people so far, some with burn injuries," Claude Hogan, a Montserrat government spokesman said.

Between 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. EDT (1700 and 1800 GMT) on Wednesday, part of the giant dome of volcanic material that has been growing inside Montserrat's Soufriere Hills volcano collapsed, dousing much of the island with ash and sending a pyroclastic flow -- a fast-moving rain of superheated gases, ash and rock -- toward the east of the island.
Authorities said seven villages along the flow burst into flames.
Hogan said there were no confirmed deaths so far. But he said one person had been seriously burned and others suffered varying degrees of burn injuries.
Officials said rescue teams were conducting house-to-house searches of the affected areas, all of them in the so-called "danger zone," which has been evacuated for 14 months.
Crewmen from a Royal Dutch Navy ship docked in Montserrat were assisting with the search.
"We're keeping our fingers crossed," Franklin Michael, permanent secretary of the island's Emergency Operations Centre, said.
Some of the people affected were residents who had refused to evacuate. Others were farmers returning to feed animals and check on their property.
Scientists monitoring the volcano reported no further intense activity by mid-day on Thursday, but warned residents to be alert and avoid the danger zone.
"We have actually been warned that the volcano could produce further large pyroclastic flows," Hogan said.
Montserrat's airport, which was evacuated on Wednesday, remained closed and was not expected to be opened for a least a couple of days, Hogan said.
A British Royal Navy ship stationed in the Caribbean was heading to the island.
The Soufriere Hills volcano roared to life in a rain of ash, rock and smoke on July 18, 1995, ending nearly four centuries of virtual dormancy.
Since then, the island's eastern end, including its capital Plymouth, has been repeatedly evacuated because of threats of eruption and Montserrat's population has shrunk from 11,000 to 6,800 people.
